stories.title: Researchers are building AI-powered robot labs. What does this mean for science?
stories.summary: Thanks to new technologies like artificial intelligence, scientists are increasingly freed from the constraints of the laboratory. It raises questions about how much humans should outsource to robots.

stories.title: Ecuador fishermen claim U.S. strike destroyed boats and crew detained
stories.summary: Fishermen working off Ecuador say they were attacked by drones, taken onboard a U.S.-flagged vessel, cuffed and handed over to Salvadoran officials. They want to know who attacked them and why.

stories.title: The challenges to providing aid in this latest Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with Heather Kerr of the International Rescue Committee about the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the challenges facing the response efforts.

stories.title: U.S. announces official 2026 FIFA World Cup roster
stories.summary: The U.S. National Men's Soccer Team announced it's official 26-player roster for the World Cup. The tournament starts in June.

stories.title: As Trump touts progress on Iran talks, major obstacles remain
stories.summary: President Trump heralded an advance in making a deal with Iran to end the war, but the way forward remains unclear.

stories.title: Sonny Rollins, a giant of jazz saxophone, had a lifelong commitment to spontaneity
stories.summary: Sonny Rollins, the jazz legend known as the Saxophone Colossus died yesterday at his home in Woodstock, N.Y. He was 95 years old and one of the last of his generation of jazz titans.
